page.title: Free Reaction Time Test Online
page.meta_description: A free reaction time test that runs in your browser. Ten trials, then your mean, median, fastest time and spread. No sign-up, nothing sent anywhere.
page.lead: Wait for the panel to change color, then click or tap as fast as you can. Ten trials, then you get your mean, median, fastest time and spread. Nothing to install, nothing sent anywhere.
page.stage_start_hint: You can also press Space or Enter.
page.stage_help: Press Space or Enter when the panel changes color.
page.median_hint: The middle value. One slip moves it less than the mean.
page.history_empty: No series yet. Kept in this browser only.
page.read_p1: Most adults land between 200 and 300 ms on a simple visual test like this one. Your device adds a little: the screen refresh, the mouse or touch screen, and the browser all take a few milliseconds, so compare yourself with yourself, on the same device.
page.read_p2: Sleep, fatigue, caffeine and the time of day all shift the result. The spread often says more than the fastest time: a steady series means your attention held from one trial to the next.
page.read_p3: This test measures a simple reaction time. It is not a diagnosis, and it is not a clinical attention test.
page.cta_title: Want the full version, in 17 languages?
page.cta_p1: The {link} keeps your history, explains each number and lets you share a result.
page.cta_p2: It is made by the team behind {upchin}, an iPhone app that helps you cut down on screen time with Apple's Screen Time.
page.footer: Open source, a single HTML file, no tracking. Your results stay in your browser's local storage.
page.too_soon_hint: Wait for the color change. Click to try this trial again.
page.spoken_too_soon: Too soon. Click to try again.
page.finished_hint: Your mean over {total} trials. Click to run a new series.

readme.title: Free reaction test online
readme.intro: A free reaction time test that runs in your browser, in a single HTML file.
readme.how: Wait for the panel to change color, then click, tap or press Space as fast as you can. After ten trials you get:
readme.def_median: **Median**: the middle value, which one slip moves less than the mean.
readme.def_spread: **Spread**: the standard deviation. Lower means steadier.
readme.def_false: **False starts**: clicks before the color change. The trial is repeated.
readme.storage: The last ten series are kept in your browser's local storage. Nothing is sent anywhere: no tracking, no external script, no sign-up.
readme.run: Open `index.html` in any browser. No build step and no dependency.
readme.reading_p1: Most adults land between 200 and 300 ms on a simple visual test like this one. The screen, the mouse or touch screen and the browser each add a few milliseconds, so compare yourself with yourself, on the same device. Sleep, fatigue, caffeine and the time of day all shift the result.
readme.reading_p2: This test measures a simple reaction time. It is not a diagnosis, and it is not a clinical attention test.
